note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Primaries held March 17, 2026.

IL-senate.statusNote: Open seat (Sen. Durbin retiring): Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton (D) faces attorney and former state GOP chair Don Tracy (R). Both nominated March 17.

IL-governor.statusNote: Gov. JB Pritzker (D) seeks a third term against 2022 rival Darren Bailey (R), who won his primary with about 54%.

candidates.name: Juliana Stratton
candidates.background: Illinois Lieutenant Governor since 2019 and a former state representative; earlier a mediator and director of the UIC Center for Public Safety and Justice. Won the March Democratic primary over Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi with Gov. Pritzker's endorsement.
priorities: Affordability and wages ($25 federal minimum wage)

cost.label: Backs a $25 federal minimum wage and a middle-class tax cut; calls affordability the top issue (WTTW questionnaire)

housing.label: Mixed: 'cutting red tape, building more' so families aren't competing with banks for homes (WTTW questionnaire)

immigration.label: 'ICE must be abolished'; supports the DREAM Act and Protecting Sensitive Locations Act (Sun-Times questionnaire)

taxes.label: Middle-class tax cut paid for by a tax increase on incomes over $1M; expanded EITC (Sun-Times questionnaire)

climate.label: Cites her record of 'urgent action on climate change' in Illinois; no detailed federal proposals published (campaign site)

education.label: Restore the Department of Education; expand Pell and federal support to trade schools (campaign site)

repro.label: Restore Roe v. Wade protections in federal law (campaign site)

democracy.label: Pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Act; reform the filibuster for voting-rights bills (Sun-Times questionnaire)

candidates.name: Don Tracy
candidates.now: Attorney; former Illinois Republican Party chair
candidates.background: Springfield attorney with a 50-year legal career; chaired the Illinois Gaming Board (2015-2019) and the Illinois Republican Party (2021-2024). Longtime outside counsel to family business Dot Foods. Won the March Republican primary with about 40%.

cost.label: Central plank: lower housing, grocery, utility, and health costs by cutting spending and regulation (campaign site)

health.label: Price transparency and cross-state-line insurance competition; opposes taxpayer-funded care for non-citizens (WTTW questionnaire)

housing.label: Expand affordable housing by removing regulatory barriers that drive prices up (campaign site)

immigration.label: Enforce the law, secure the border, supports the SAVE Act and ending birthright citizenship by amendment; backs a 'structured path to legal residency' (21st Show)

taxes.label: 'Keep more of what you earn'; opposes tax increases on working families; flags Illinois property-tax burden (WTTW questionnaire)

climate.label: 'All-of-the-above, common sense' energy: lower costs, energy independence (campaign site)

safety.label: Backs law enforcement and accountability-focused policies to make communities safer (campaign site)

repro.label: Abortion law should be left to the states; supports the Hyde Amendment with rape/incest/life exceptions (21st Show)

democracy.label: Supports voter photo ID and proof-of-citizenship registration (SAVE Act) (21st Show)

controversies.label: 2019 inspector general alleged prohibited political activity while Gaming Board chair; the state Ethics Commission ruled in 2025 that investigators failed to prove a violation (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: JB Pritzker
candidates.background: Governor since 2019, seeking a third term; a win would make him the first Illinois governor with three terms since Jim Thompson. Billionaire businessman and venture capitalist before office; beat Darren Bailey by about 13 points in 2022.
priorities: Standing up to the Trump administration

cost.label: Eliminated the state grocery tax, doubled the child tax credit, raised the minimum wage to $15 (WhereTheyStand)

health.label: Signed the $35 insulin cap; medical-debt relief erased ~$345M for 270,000 residents (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Mixed: 2026 BUILD plan relaxes zoning, legalizes ADUs, cuts parking minimums AND adds $15K down-payment assistance (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Banned private immigration detention and police-ICE deportation cooperation; resists federal ICE operations (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Pushed a graduated income tax raising rates on high earners (voters rejected it in 2020); doubled the gas tax for infrastructure (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Signed CEJA: carbon-free power by 2045, 50% renewables by 2040; 2026 law adds 2+ GW of new nuclear (Wikipedia)

education.label: Large K-12 and higher-ed funding increases across two terms (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Signed and defends the SAFE-T Act ending cash bail, paired with law-enforcement investment (WhereTheyStand)

repro.label: Signed the Reproductive Health Act making abortion a 'fundamental right' in Illinois (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Co-founded Governors Safeguarding Democracy; created an Illinois commission on federal overreach (Wikipedia)

controversies.label: ~$230K property-tax break on a mansion made 'uninhabitable' by removing toilets (repaid); recorded on the 2008 Blagojevich wiretaps, later apologized (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Darren Bailey
candidates.background: Southern Illinois farmer and former state senator; the 2022 Republican nominee for governor, back for a 2026 rematch after winning the primary with about 54%. Co-founded a family farm operation and a private Christian school. This cycle he emphasizes economics over social issues.
priorities: Cut energy costs; 'Illinois DOGE' spending audits

cost.label: 'Put more money back in the pockets of everyday Illinoisans'; cut utility bills; property-tax relief (campaign site)

immigration.label: Mixed-enforcement: opposes Illinois sanctuary laws while criticizing federal ICE operations in Cook County (WhereTheyStand)

taxes.label: Cap property taxes, lower taxes overall, 'Illinois DOGE' efficiency audits (Capitol News Illinois)

climate.label: Repeal CEJA, the 2021 clean-energy law, blaming it for utility-price increases (Capitol News Illinois)

education.label: School choice: 'empower parents'; classrooms should teach fundamentals, 'not political agendas' (campaign site)

safety.label: Repeal the SAFE-T Act ('radical, pro-criminal'), restore stricter bail, back law enforcement (campaign site)

repro.label: Record of supporting a near-total ban with life-of-mother exception only; 2026 homepage still pledges to 'defend the sanctity of life' (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Refused to acknowledge Biden's 2020 victory, citing fraud claims (Wikipedia)

controversies.label: Removed from the Illinois House floor in 2020 for refusing to wear a mask; 2017 comment comparing abortion to the Holocaust (Wikipedia)
